question: Why do severe stomach and gut problems often affect the whole body?

options.A: Routine administration of broad-spectrum oral antibiotics
options.B: Excessive daily water intake by the affected patient
options.C: Disruption of the normal gut barrier and blood supply
options.D: Increased physical activity during the acute illness phase

explanation: When the gut wall or its blood supply fails, toxins and fluid shift quickly, affecting the entire body. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h1)

question: What usually happens when a patient delays seeking care for a severe stomach illness?

options.B: Complete normalization of electrolyte laboratory values
options.C: Immediate localized symptoms without systemic effects
options.D: Severe secondary complications requiring urgent care

explanation: Delaying care allows a localized gut issue to spread and cause multi-system problems. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h1)

question: Throwing up for a long time due to a blocked stomach outlet usually causes which imbalance?
explanation: Losing acidic stomach contents leaves excess bicarbonate in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h2)

question: Severe watery diarrhea that causes a big loss of lower gut fluids mainly leads to which imbalance?

options.A: Excessive production of potassium by the colon
options.B: Retention of sodium causing severe fluid overload
options.C: Loss of bicarbonate leading to metabolic acidosis

explanation: Lower gut fluids contain lots of bicarbonate, so losing them depletes the body's acid buffers. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h2)

question: Dark, tarry stools known as melena usually mean bleeding is coming from where?
explanation: As blood passes all the way through the GI tract, it gets digested and turns the stool dark and tarry. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h3)

question: A patient with a bleeding duodenal ulcer has cold skin, a fast pulse, and confusion. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for complete laboratory blood profile results
options.C: Administer a large oral dose of liquid antacids
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward

explanation: Signs of shock mean the body is losing fluid volume, so replacing fluids quickly is vital to restore blood flow. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h3)

question: A rigid, board-like stomach and pain when you press and let go are classic signs of what condition?
explanation: When the lining of the abdominal cavity gets inflamed from leaked gut contents, the muscles tighten up. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h4)

question: During a complete bowel blockage, what causes the bowel wall to tear or perforate?

options.A: Ischemia and necrosis from prolonged high pressure inside
options.B: Sudden relaxation of the muscular layers of the stomach
options.C: Direct ingestion of sharp foreign bodies in the diet
options.D: Rapid overgrowth of normal colonic flora and gas

explanation: High pressure inside a blocked bowel cuts off blood supply, leading to tissue death and a ruptured wall. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h4)

question: Swelling in the limbs (peripheral edema) from long-term poor nutrient absorption is mainly caused by low levels of which blood protein?
explanation: Low protein levels drop the pressure inside blood vessels, causing fluid to leak out into the tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why do patients who have had a large part of their small bowel removed suffer from severe nutritional deficiencies?

options.A: Loss of mucosal surface area prevents adequate nutrient absorption
options.B: Bile production by the gallbladder is permanently halted
options.C: The liver increases its clearance of circulating vitamins
options.D: The stomach stops producing hydrochloric acid entirely

explanation: The small intestine is where most nutrients are absorbed, so losing length means the body loses that absorbing power. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h5)

question: The buildup of which specific waste product is the main cause of liver-related brain confusion (hepatic encephalopathy)?
explanation: A failing liver cannot turn nitrogen waste into urea, letting ammonia build up and affect the brain. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is the main feature of hepatorenal syndrome in advanced liver disease?

options.A: Direct physical obstruction of the ureters by liver scar tissue
options.B: Severe bacterial infection ascending from the urinary bladder
options.C: Permanent destruction of the renal glomeruli by immune complexes
options.D: Functional kidney failure caused by intense blood vessel narrowing

explanation: Changes in blood flow cause the kidneys to stop working properly even though there is no structural damage to the kidneys themselves. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which sign usually gives the earliest warning that a patient is heading into shock from fluid loss?
explanation: The heart beats faster to keep blood circulating well before blood pressure actually drops. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h7)

question: A patient recovering from bowel surgery has a growing stomach size and feels nauseous. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a comprehensive abdominal assessment and check vital signs
options.B: Document the findings as a normal postoperative response
options.C: Encourage the patient to drink large amounts of oral water
options.D: Administer a strong laxative to stimulate bowel movement

explanation: Getting vital signs and checking the abdomen provides the facts needed before reporting or taking further action. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h7)

question: What is the main reason for putting a tube through the nose into the stomach (nasogastric tube) for a bowel obstruction?

options.A: Administer large volumes of oral contrast for imaging scans
options.B: Prevent the absorption of toxic medications in the duodenum
options.C: Deliver high-caloric liquid meals directly into the stomach
options.D: Decompress the gastrointestinal tract by removing air and fluid

explanation: Suctioning through the tube relieves pressure inside the gut, easing vomiting and reducing the risk of aspiration. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h8)

question: Why must a patient with acute peritonitis be kept strictly nothing-by-mouth (NPO)?

options.A: To prepare the stomach lining for routine endoscopic viewing
options.B: To stop the kidneys from producing concentrated urine output
options.C: To prevent stimulating gastrointestinal secretions and peristalsis
options.D: To ensure the patient loses excess weight during hospital stay

explanation: Resting the gut keeps movement low, which helps reduce pain and stops the infection from spreading. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h8)
